ratings.note: Every booking hits the 1.5 s silent wait (probe 6/20: page unchanged at 0 and 800 ms); impact is doubt and a likely second press; recurs each booking. s=3. The cancellation a second press causes is rated separately (B-010).

Only cancelled bookings (including accidental ones via B-010); a misread means a wasted trip and being turned away (impact 3); recurs on each view. s=4, rated 3 because the screenshot shows the red 'Status: cancelled... not on the gate's list' line prominently right under the reference, so most readers will see it.
Only when a hold lapses; at the final step the alert gives no next step and the slot row shows a dash, though a small 'Change slot' link is next to it (screenshot); recurs per expiry. s=3.
Screen-reader users only; the limits are still in the checkbox names ('Rubble (up to four bags)', 'Mattresses (up to two)') and readable in browse mode, so practical effect is trivial; recurs. s=1.

Every done page lacks day/time/vehicle; it matters for residents who forget or check at the gate with poor signal, a common case; arriving at the wrong time means being turned away, partly mitigated by the evening reminder; recurs whenever consulted. s=3.

Only slow or interrupted residents (older users, screen readers, multitasking scene) exceed the hold; losing a scarce slot at the last step is significant; for slow users it recurs on every attempt and cannot be learned around. s=3. Same root as B-012/B-026, rated consistently.

Every booking passes step 2 without seeing the day/time (screenshot); impact is mild recall load; recurs. s=3, rated 2 because the confirm page repeats the day and slot before anything is committed, so a wrong choice is caught there.
Low-vision and outdoor phone users on 'few' slots meet ~3.0:1 (light) / 3.4:1 (dark) text, failing 1.4.3; the tag is informational, slots remain bookable; not overcome by learning. s=2.

Every car booking (primary group) sees an unqualified 'Permit number' field after choosing Car (screenshot); most will leave it blank and Next works, but some will stop or call; occasional users meet it each visit. s=3.

Residents whose plans change (declared core task); the only route is a weekday phone call, i.e. a support contact, and impossible evenings/weekends when they book (impact 3); every change, not learnable around. s=4.
Every Change slot / Back to the slots use (probes 7, 17, 25) lands on Today with no selection; extra steps and a real risk of picking a slot on the wrong day; recurs each time. s=3.
Keyboard/screen-reader users with a vehicle-step error; focus goes to body, not announced, though the next Tab reaches Car; recurs. s=2.
Same hidden hold as B-003/B-012: slow or interrupted residents lose the slot without warning; significant loss at the last step; recurs for them. s=3.
Desktop users only (minority); a third of each row is empty at 1280 px but slots remain fully usable; persistent but harmless. s=1.
Only residents amending waste at the check step; 'Change vehicle' works if guessed, otherwise an incomplete list; recurs on visits. s=2.
Today is the default day and same-day booking is common in the declared scene; past slots look free and are rejected only after the whole flow (probe 46); recurs daily. s=3.

Every day change shows a blank Slots area with the old date for ~0.9-1.3 s (probes 2, 31); mild ambiguity; recurs. s=3, rated 2 because the gap is about a second and slots appear before most users would act on the blank.
Van/trailer owners without a permit; help says 'apply on the council site' with no link, forcing an external search; once they hold a permit it no longer matters. s=2.
Five-minute hold, never stated or extendable (2.2.1); only bookings over 5 minutes, but those are older/AT users who will hit it repeatedly; slot lost at the last press, details kept. s=3.

Van/trailer owners; the permit lead-time explanation hides behind an unlabelled (i) box (screenshot), risking a missed two-day lead time; the visible Permit field still signals a permit is needed, and once learned the issue is gone. s=2.
Every vehicle-step visitor sees the (i) box styled like a fourth vehicle option (screenshot); a mistaken tap only opens help; learned once. s=2.
Van/trailer bookings with a missing or mistyped permit; error appears only after details and the 1.5 s wait, on a page without the field, needing a round trip; recurs per attempt. s=3.
Only late booking errors; the summary item has no link, but Change slot / Change vehicle links sit directly below in 'Your booking' (expired screenshot); recurs. s=2.
Many slots on most days carry 'Few left', which makes little sense for a one-vehicle slot; causes hesitation rather than error; understood or ignored after first use. s=2.
Every resident sees an unqualified Permit number field before choosing a vehicle (screenshot); most car users leave it blank, some stop or call; occasional users meet it each visit. s=3.

Occurs on a repeat press within 1.5 s, made likely by the silent wait; the button turns into 'Cancel booking' and the booking is silently cancelled under a 'Booked' heading (probe v3-F), so the resident is turned away; any submission can trigger it. s=4.
Same gap as B-024: the declared change-slot task requires a weekday phone call (support contact) and cannot be done evenings or weekends; every change. s=4.
Screen-reader and keyboard users on three controls; pressed state is still announced, but one-of-many is not conveyed and every slot is a tab stop; not overcome by learning. s=2.
